newsitem.title: JAPAN: JAPAN INSURERS RACE TO DRAFT PLAN FOR FAILED FIRM.
newsitem.headline: JAPAN INSURERS RACE TO DRAFT PLAN FOR FAILED FIRM.

text.p: The Life Insurance Association of Japan said on Thursday it is stepping up its efforts to draft a plan to wind up failed insurer Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, but industry sources said the plan may not be ready in time for the association's board meeting on June 20.

An association spokesman said the industry body has not yet mapped out details of the plan, although it finished its inspection of Nissan Mutual's financial condition early in June. He gave no further details.

Industry sources said that, while the association is working hard to finalise the scheme by the June 20 meeting, it faces a difficult task because, as its inspection revealed, Nissan Life's actual liabilities were even bigger than earlier expected, exceeding its assets by around 300 billion yen.

A senior official of the Ministry of Finance (MOF) recently said that it may ask life insurers to approve an increase in the contribution from an industry fund to a new firm that would take over Nissan Life policies.

The Policyholders Protection Fund, with contributions from 44 life insurers, can presently inject up to 200 billion yen into a company taking over the policies of a failed insurer. The MOF official said this amount could be increased if the rules were changed.

He added that it is possible under present laws to change the high returns Nissan Life guaranteed on its individual pension policies if the policies are taken over by another firm as part of the scheme to wind up the failed insurer.
Industry sources said, however, that life insurers have been opposing MOF's request to boost their contribution to the Policyholders Protection Fund. Thursday, 12 June 1997 08:39:35 RTRS nT129864
